papers.title: Stability boundary of neutron-dark matter mixed stars
papers.authors: Xiao-Ding Zhou, 小丁 周, Tian-Shun Chen, 天舜 陈, Si-Man Wu, 思熳 吴, Kilar Zhang and 弘 张
papers.summary: In terms of the stability of two-fluid star models, we rigorously prove the equivalence between the emergence of a zero-frequency radial oscillation mode and the static critical-curve criterion for mixed stars, after briefly reviewing the hybrid star case. This establishes a sufficient-condition relation between two independently developed stability criteria. Although this connection has often been implicitly assumed in previous studies on mixed stars, it has rarely been demonstrated explicitly. Our derivation can be extended to general multi-fluid systems. As an example, we consider dark matter-admixed neutron star models and show that their stability boundary differs from that of single-fluid stars. In this case, stable configurations form a surface in the three-dimensional parameter space spanned by the central pressure, mass, and radius, giving rise to a class of stable mixed stars. This class includes ''twin stars'' with identical masses and radii but distinct internal compositions and structures. These results provide a useful framework for interpreting compact star observations and constraining dark matter properties through astrophysical measurements.

papers.title: Frequencies spectra and gravitational ringing around Hayward-AdS black holes immersed in a string fluid*
papers.authors: G. Mustafa, Faisal Javed, Dhruba Jyoti Gogoi, S. K. Maurya, Akram Ali and Farruh Atamurotov
papers.summary: We investigate the dynamics of test particles in a Hayward–AdS black hole with string fluid, with particular emphasis on how the relevant parameters influence particle motion. The stability of circular orbits is studied using the effective potential method, which yields analytic expressions for the particle energy and angular momentum in terms of the black hole parameters. The effects of these parameters on the innermost stable circular orbit and the effective force are also examined. In addition, we calculate the pericenter precession frequency and investigate the small oscillatory motion of a particle around a stable orbit, examining how the corresponding frequency is modified by the black hole parameters. We further compare particle dynamics in the Hayward–AdS spacetime with string fluid to those in the Hayward–AdS, the Hayward Reissner Nordstrom, and the conventional Hayward black holes. Lastly, we examine the influence of the string fluid and the Hayward parameter on the quasinormal spectrum and the time-domain dynamics of electromagnetic perturbations, and find that these two terms have reciprocal effects on the quasinormal scale.

papers.title: A comprehensive cosmographic and thermodynamic analysis of non-metric-matter coupled gravity
papers.authors: M. Zeeshan Gul, Shamraiza Shabbir, Fei Ni, 菲 倪 and Muhannad Mohammed Alfehaid
papers.summary: The main objective of this manuscript is to explore the viable cosmological bounce solutions in the background of gravity, where Q denotes the non-metricity scalar describing the curvature of spacetime, represents the matter-Lagrangian density, and T is the trace of the energy-momentum tensor. For this purpose, we consider an isotropic and homogeneous universe with bulk viscous fluid to examine the implications of this framework on the dynamics of the early universe. The central focus of this work is to uncover the role of bulk viscosity on the cosmic evolution, especially in non-singular bounces. Furthermore, we investigate the behavior of various cosmological parameters to identify the viable bounce solutions. We find that the positive energy density, negative pressure profile and violation of energy conditions (ECs) support the realization of a cosmological bounce. These results emphasize the importance of bulk viscosity in shaping the cosmic dynamics. We demonstrate that system's entropy evolution satisfies the second law of thermodynamics, confirming its thermodynamic consistency over time. Moreover, the examination of cosmographic parameters and adiabatic sound speed demonstrates the model's kinematic feasibility and stability. Our findings imply that gravity stands as a consistent and alternative theory for standard cosmology, providing a significant theoretical framework to study the gravitational interactions. This modified gravitational theory (MGT) successfully accommodates important aspect of cosmic evolutions and offers a new perspective on geometric and coupling effects that may govern the dynamics of the universe beyond the predictions of general relativity.

papers.title: Photon regions, shadow observables and constraints from M87* of a Kerr-Newman-like black hole in Bumblebee gravity surrounded by plasma*
papers.authors: Jian-Peng Zhang, 健鹏 张, Yu Zhang, 钰 张, Li Han and 力 韩
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the photon regions, shadow, and observational constraints of a Kerr-Newman-like black hole in Bumblebee gravity within a plasma medium. Using a specific non-homogeneous power-law plasma model to ensure the separability of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, we derive the null geodesic equations, analyze the photon regions, and construct the black hole shadow. Furthermore, we introduce two sets of shadow observables to systematically analyze the distinct effects of each physical parameter (spin a, charge , Lorentz-violating parameter ℓ, and plasma parameter k) on the shadow geometry. Specifically, we find that a and ℓ mainly enhance the distortion of the shadow, whereas and k primarily lead to radial shrinkage. In addition, a brief evaluation of the energy emission rate shows that increasing these parameters generally suppresses the emission peak. Finally, by modeling M87* as a charged, rotating black hole in Bumblebee gravity surrounded by plasma, we constrain the physical parameters using observations from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT). For a fixed viewing angle of , the angular diameter narrows the viable parameter space, while the circularity deviation and axis ratio satisfy the EHT limits. This suggests that the charged, rotating black hole in Bumblebee gravity surrounded by plasma may be a candidate for real astrophysical black holes.

papers.title: Tuning a rotating black hole spectrum with dark matter halo: quasibound states, scalar cloud, black hole bomb and superradiant scattering
papers.summary: We investigate the spectral dynamics of a rotating black hole embedded in a Dehnen dark matter halo, in which quasibound states and superradiant scattering jointly characterize the physical response of the system. Starting from an exact Schwarzschild–Dehnen solution, we construct its rotating counterpart via the Newman–Janis algorithm, thereby obtaining a consistent axisymmetric geometry that incorporates the influence of a structured halo. Through its inner slope parameter γ, the Dehnen profile introduces a controlled deformation of both the near-horizon and asymptotic regions of the spacetime. Using the analytical asymptotic matching method, we derive the quasibound-state spectrum and show that the real part of the frequency retains a hydrogen-like structure but is systematically shifted by the leading-order halo correction proportional to . In particular, denser, more extended, and cuspier halos strengthen the binding of the quasibound states, lower the critical mass required for the onset of instability, and typically suppress the growth rate of the black hole bomb. In the scattering sector, we obtain an analytic expression for the superradiant amplification factor and find that the same halo properties that strengthen the binding effects also tend to narrow the superradiant window. These results demonstrate that quasibound states and superradiant scattering are complementary manifestations of a unified spectral structure, with the Dehnen halo acting as an environmental tuner that directly imprints its properties onto both the resonance spectrum and the energy-extraction channels of the rotating black hole.

papers.title: Rational orbits and gravitational waves in static spherical spacetimes: an open-source numerical framework*
papers.authors: Dan Li, 丹 李, Shiyang Hu, 诗杨 胡, Chen Deng, 晨 邓, Shijie Tan, 世杰 谭, Guansheng He and 观圣 贺
papers.summary: Timelike orbits constitute a crucial probe for exploring the intrinsic properties of curved spacetimes, and the accompanying gravitational radiation signals provide a direct window into strong field gravity. In this paper, we develop a versatile computational framework based on Mathematica and the OpenMP parallel architecture to simulate the rational orbits of timelike particles and their gravitational radiation in static spherically symmetric spacetimes. Specifically, with only the user defined covariant metric as input, this numerical tool can efficiently calculate rational orbits for various configurations, as well as the corresponding gravitational wave polarization states and characteristic strains. The package presented here provides an efficient and comprehensive tool for investigating the properties of curved spacetimes and their potential observational signatures. To demonstrate the reliability and capability of our code, we apply it to the Schwarzschild spacetime as a test case, illustrating its functionality in several key aspects, including the effective potential, stable orbital regions, rational and irrational orbits, and gravitational wave signals. Furthermore, we show that the gravitational waves emitted by an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral system composed of an intermediate mass black hole and the Galactic Center supermassive black hole could be detected by future space detectors.

papers.title: Polarization modes of gravitational waves in general symmetric teleparallel gravity*
papers.authors: Yu-Qi Dong, 雨奇 董, Xiao-Bin Lai, 小斌 赖, Yu-Zhi Fan, 雨知 范, Yu-Xiao Liu and 玉孝 刘
papers.summary: This study investigates the polarization modes of gravitational waves within the most general symmetric teleparallel gravity theory that allows for second-order field equations. We consider scenarios where test particles either carry or do not carry a hypermomentum charge. Our findings reveal the existence of tensor, vector, and scalar modes of gravitational waves. First, the theory supports the + and × tensor modes propagating at the speed of light. Second, in the case where particles do not carry hypermomentum, vector modes propagating at the speed of light exist only within a very specific parameter space. However, when particles do carry hypermomentum, there are two shear modes that propagate at the speed of light, while the vector-x and vector-y modes emerge only under very specific conditions. Third, in the presence of hypermomentum, there is always a longitudinal mode propagating at the speed of light. The universal existence of the shear modes and the longitudinal mode in the presence of hypermomentum is a key feature of symmetric teleparallel gravity, distinguishing it from the Riemannian framework through gravitational wave polarization detection. We also analyze the polarization modes in two widely studied special theories: f(Q) theory and quadratic non-metricity theory.

papers.title: Topological signatures in Kerr-Sen AdS black hole thermodynamics
papers.authors: Mohd Rehan, Md Sabir Ali and Sushant G. Ghosh
papers.summary: Black hole thermodynamics and topology have emerged as a robust foundation for a coordinate-independent understanding of phase transitions. Using both Duan’s topological current theory and a novel complex residue method, we conduct a topological study of the Kerr-Sen AdS black hole arising in heterotic string theory. Specifically, we identify the zero points corresponding to on-shell black hole states and calculate their winding numbers to determine the global topological charge by constructing the generalized off-shell free energy and examining the corresponding vector field in a parametric space. Our analysis reveals that the Kerr-Sen AdS black hole exhibits three distinct thermodynamic phases—small, intermediate, and large black hole branches—characterized by critical points with winding numbers , , and , respectively, culminating in a total topological charge . Significantly, this topological number remains invariant under variations of the dilaton charge parameter, indicating that the dilaton field does not alter the fundamental topological class established for Kerr-AdS and RN-AdS black holes. However, the rotation parameter proves crucial in determining the phase structure and the emergence of multiple critical points. We systematically examine three limiting configurations: the full Kerr-Sen AdS spacetime, the GMGHS AdS limit ( ), and the asymptotically flat Kerr-Sen case ( ). The GMGHS AdS black hole yields a vanishing total topological charge, with winding numbers and canceling each other, while the Kerr-Sen black hole ( ) similarly exhibits despite possessing two distinct phase branches. Furthermore, we propose a novel approach by analytically continuing the thermodynamic characterization to the complex plane. The resulting complex function, derived from the off-shell Gibbs free energy, possesses isolated singular points whose residues directly encode the winding numbers. Our results indicate that topology offers profound insights into black hole phase transitions, with potential implications for understanding holographic dualities.

papers.title: Observable thin accretion disk around a self-dual black hole in loop quantum gravity*
papers.authors: Tursunali Xamidov, Javokhir Sharipov and Sanjar Shaymatov
papers.summary: In this paper, we study a self-dual black hole (BH) in loop quantum gravity (LQG) by analyzing both timelike and null geodesics. Using observational data from Mercury’s perihelion shift and the orbit of the S2 star around Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*), we derive constraints on the polymeric function P. We also investigate photon trajectories near the self-dual BH under various scenarios to assess their observational relevance. Finally, we examine the properties of accretion disks around the self-dual BH in LQG, including their direct and secondary images. We further study the redshift and observed energy-flux distribution across the accretion disk, as measured by distant observers at different inclination angles. Our findings provide new insights into the physical nature and accretion properties of self-dual BHs in LQG and their possible observational consequences.

papers.title: Photon spheres and shadows of black holes with modified entropy-inspired metrics*
papers.authors: Fang Liu, 芳 刘, Yu-Bo Ma, 宇波 马, Yun-Zhi Du, 云芝 杜, Huai-Fan Li and 怀繁 李
papers.summary: Starting from the first law of black hole thermodynamics, we establish an explicit correspondence between the corrected entropy and the metric function under the condition of fixed black hole energy and horizon location. Using the corrected metric, we then compute the photon sphere radius and shadow size, demonstrating that different entropy corrections produce characteristic optical shifts. By comparing these results with Event Horizon Telescope observations of Sgr A*, we constrain the parameter range associated with the corrected entropy. This analysis provides a feasible approach for testing generalized entropy frameworks and probing deviations from the Bekenstein--Hawking area law.

papers.title: Astrophysical origins of TeV features in the cosmic-ray lepton spectrum*
papers.authors: Zhen Xie, 禛 谢, Ruizhi Yang and 睿智 杨
papers.summary: Precise measurements of high-energy cosmic-ray electrons and positrons have revealed spectral features that are difficult to reproduce with a single smooth power-law background. The rising positron fraction measured by PAMELA and AMS-02, together with the all-electron excess reported by ATIC and the high-precision all-electron spectrum measured by DAMPE, has motivated interpretations ranging from nearby astrophysical accelerators to dark-matter annihilation or decay. In this work, we revisit the conventional diffuse electron background and the possible contribution from nearby pulsars within a common propagation framework. The diffuse component is modeled using GALPROP configurations calibrated against cosmic-ray nuclei and diffuse gamma-ray observations. We then use the Green-function solution for nearby discrete sources with radiative losses to study pulsar contributions with both burst-like and continuous injection histories, including the effect of stochastic inverse-Compton cooling on the propagated spectra. We also use the highest-energy DAMPE data points as an illustrative case to compare possible local-source contributions from pulsars and supernova-remnant-like burst sources. The spectral shape of such features provides a useful diagnostic for distinguishing physically plausible nearby-source features from more exotic interpretations.

papers.title: Observational constraints on fractional holographic dark energy in the light of DESI DR2*
papers.authors: Qihong Huang, 启洪 黄, Yuchen Zhang, 宇辰 张, Bing Xu, 兵 徐, Kaituo Zhang and 开拓 张
papers.summary: Based on the fractional entropy from fractional quantum mechanics, fractional holographic dark energy (FHDE) has been proposed with the Hubble horizon as the IR cutoff (FHDEH). We extend this framework by adopting the future event horizon and the particle horizon as the IR cutoff and proposing the FHDEF and FHDEP models. Using the SN+OHD+DESI DR2 dataset to constrain these models, we find that all three models provide a marginally lower compared to ΛCDM but without significant preference according to AIC and BIC. When CMB distance priors are included, the FHDEH and FHDEP models are strongly ruled out. We further analyze the cosmological evolution for these models, and find that only the FHDEF model predicts nearly identical evolutions of and to those of the ΛCDM model across cosmic history, but its deceleration parameter q deviates from the ΛCDM model in the future, indicating richer late time dynamics beyond the standard ΛCDM cosmology.

papers.title: Prospects for studying the WHγ process in pp collisions at the LHC*
papers.authors: Youpeng Wu, 友鹏 吴, Jie Xiao, 杰 肖, Andrew Michael Levin, Qiang Li and 强 李
papers.summary: The Standard Model of particle physics, although remarkably successful, leaves several major questions unanswered, continuing to motivate searches for new phenomena. Multiboson interactions involving the Higgs boson are of particular interest as probes of the electroweak Lagrangian, where potential new physics may reside. In this work, we present a study of the associated production of a W boson, a Higgs boson, and a photon in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). Monte Carlo simulations are performed to model both the signal and background processes, and detector effects are included according to CMS specifications. Boosted decision trees are employed to optimize the event selection and enhance signal–background discrimination. We estimate that, with an integrated luminosity of 440 fb−1, the expected significance for the process is 0.63σ, increasing to a projected 1.64σ at the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC).
